questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
Have three brakes: one in the front, one in the rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One brake is on the front wheel, and one is on the rear wheel.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't worry about checking the tire pressure.
Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
The lender will make sure the brakes work so you don't have to.
Give yourself an extra cushion of space when riding to allow more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself an extra cushion of space when riding to allow more time to react.
questions.explanation: Check the borrowed motorcycle the same way you check your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike. Keep extra space between you and other vehicles so you have time to stop.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Maintain a space cushion between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to monitor traffic behind you.
Look for opportunities to squeeze through the stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a space cushion between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle approaches too quickly from behind.

questions.question: Riding gloves are often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as necessary.
Does not have any markings or tags.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as necessary.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see far to the sides for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels with the maker's name, instructions, and information about safety standards.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete
questions.explanation: Many surfaces create poor traction for tires: wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, you should look at all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shininess
questions.explanation: Check your air pressure, tread, and general wear before each ride. How shiny the tires are is not important for safety.

questions.question: If you are feeling tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: Like cars, motorcycles have blind spots. When switching lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, lights, turn signals, mirrors, brakes, clutch, throttle, and horn.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out suddenly and hit you.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly and hit you.
questions.explanation: A driver could pull out of a parking space without looking and hit you. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: What material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: The driver cannot see you if you ride in their blind spot. The vehicle may also block your way if you need to escape a hazard.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: What is a benefit of smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle?

options.text: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
You should not do it near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Smoothly downshifting allows the engine to help slow your motorcycle. Use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid accidents?

options.text: Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Only signal when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a rectangular sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white and black lettering. These regulatory signs tell you the rules you must follow on the road.

questions.question: What type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing so other drivers can see you and your motorcycle more easily.

questions.question: A helmet should fit how to give the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. It should meet DOT and state safety standards.

questions.question: What helps you avoid a crash?

options.text: Keep your intentions unknown from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals and brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What happens if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is acceptable as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is acceptable as long as no vehicles are near you.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could end up in another lane or off the road. Be careful when turning.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows down a motorcycle. Note that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights, so other drivers may not know you are slowing down.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Eyeballing the tire is a good method.
It is best to squeeze the tire.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire may look fine even when it is not filled properly, so looking at it is not enough.
